reasoning_traces.think:
The ranking lasso introduces an L1 penalty on pairwise team ability differences, effectively shrinking similar abilities toward equality. This produces natural groupings or tiers without requiring pre-defined clusters. The Bradley–Terry model provides the probabilistic framework for match outcomes, while the adaptive weights stabilize estimation by leveraging initial MLEs. The ties extension allows modeling of draw outcomes using cumulative links. The optimization problem splits into smooth and convex components via augmented Lagrangian methods, enabling efficient computation. The hybrid approach refines groupings post-shrinkage with unpenalized MLEs. Failure modes include divergence in adaptive weights for extreme teams and instability in λ selection across seasons. The model’s strength lies in balancing interpretability and predictive accuracy, especially in small-sample regimes.
